purpose: Triptorelin is mainly used to treat advanced prostate cancer in men by lowering testosterone levels, which helps slow cancer growth. It is also used for conditions like endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and in some cases to help with precocious puberty (early puberty in children). Your doctor may also use it for other hormone-related conditions.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes hormones that signal the production of testosterone or estrogen. Triptorelin works by overstimulating those hormone signals at first, and then essentially turning them off over time. This causes the body to produce much less testosterone (in men) or estrogen (in women), which helps treat hormone-driven conditions like prostate cancer or endometriosis.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes or hot flushes are very common. Men may notice decreased sex drive, erection problems, or fatigue. Women may experience irregular or stopped periods, vaginal dryness, or mood changes. Injection site redness or soreness, headache, and sweating are also common. Some people feel a temporary worsening of symptoms in the first few weeks of treatment.
warnings: In the first week or two of treatment, there can be a temporary 'flare' where symptoms briefly get worse before they get better — this is especially important for prostate cancer patients to know about. This medication can weaken your bones over time, so talk to your doctor about bone health. It can affect blood sugar and increase the risk of diabetes or heart problems, especially in men. Do not use this medication if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor about all your medications before starting.
typical_dosing: Triptorelin is given as an injection by a healthcare provider — you do not give this one to yourself at home. Depending on the form prescribed, it may be given once a month (3.75 mg), every 3 months (11.25 mg), or every 6 months (22.5 mg). Your doctor will decide which schedule is right for you based on your condition.
